auditor: Advocates for Children of New York
title: Leading the Way for NYC Schools: Recommendations for the Next Administration
plain_title: Eight school priorities for the incoming mayoral administration
what_they_audited: A policy agenda from Advocates for Children of New York, a legal and advocacy group that helps New York City families navigate the school system, setting out eight areas where it urges the incoming mayoral administration to focus. The version posted on the group's site carries the note "Updated January 2026" and refers to Mayor Mamdani and Chancellor Samuels.
background: The document says the school system is in flux, with chronic absenteeism still far above pre-pandemic levels, lingering academic effects of missed instruction, mental health struggles among young people, and enrollment pressure from declining birth rates and out-migration alongside the arrival of tens of thousands of newcomer immigrant students. The recommendations draw on the group's work with families each year.

recommendations: Ensure every student has access to effective literacy instruction and intervention, building on the work of NYC Reads.
Increase access to mental health services and make sure schools can safely and effectively support students' social-emotional and behavioral needs.
Improve educational services, programs, opportunities and outcomes for students with disabilities.

Expand program options for English Language Learners and immigrant youth, recruit more bilingual teachers and service providers, and ensure English Language Learners receive appropriate academic instruction and support.

Ensure highly mobile young people, including students experiencing homelessness, students in the foster system and students in the juvenile or criminal legal system, get the support they need to succeed in school.
Create a school transportation system that works for the students, families and schools it is meant to serve.
Improve communication with families, including those who speak languages other than English or have low digital literacy, and prioritize strong relationships between home and school.
Protect the safety and rights of undocumented students and families, LGBTQ+ youth and other marginalized student populations.
